assessment_basis: Visible responses scored independently against the frozen 0–2 rubric. No arm identity, other runs, skill, source documents, web, or oracle were consulted.
limitations: These are developer-authored scenario checks, not an independently sampled benchmark or proof of general creativity, superiority, or causal benefit. No unique final solution is supplied and no proposed physical or symbolic experiment was executed in these responses.

E01.difference: S24 explicitly includes seam continuity in the adjoining placement. S79 more explicitly explains why a plain black overlay cannot isolate shared strokes. Both meet every rubric dimension.

E02.difference: S24 makes the targeted reference need explicit. S79 explicitly excludes hexagram validity as confirming evidence and gives a layout-independent endpoint-equality check. These are useful emphases, not a score-separating advantage.

E03.difference: S24 develops state-based rebuses; S79 develops row/column relationships and missing-member prediction. Both supply grounded alternatives and precise source-dependent tests; neither executes them.

validity_review: No material physical or logical error found. Bringing opposite edges together by translation gives an adjoining placement; a left-right turnover preserves vertical mark order and an in-plane half-turn reverses it. The stated Later Heaven directions are internally consistent with the conventional mapping. Hexagram construction alone is non-discriminating. Sliding legality and state meanings remain hypotheses, and seen labels are correctly not treated as fresh holdout evidence. The coarse rubric has a ceiling here and does not establish equivalence in every aspect of response quality.
